title: Game Day Pizza Sliders
seoTitle: Game Day Pizza Sliders | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Pepperoni slider buns with melted cheese for ten
subtitle: Pepperoni slider buns with melted cheese for ten
description: Hawaiian rolls are split, layered with pepperoni, mozzarella, and pizza sauce, then baked until the tops turn golden and cheese pulls in long strings. Brush with garlic butter and serve with extra marinara for dunking.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Game Day Pizza Sliders in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep the roll base
steps.instruction: Slice entire roll packages horizontally without separating individual rolls. Place bottom halves in two foil-lined 9x13 pans so they fit snugly side by side.

steps.title: Layer the filling
steps.instruction: Spread pizza sauce on bottom halves, then layer pepperoni and mozzarella evenly so every slider gets cheese and meat—not just the center pieces.

steps.title: Cover and bake covered
steps.instruction: Replace top halves, cover tightly with foil, and bake at 350°F for 15 minutes until cheese melts and rolls soften into one connected block. Target oven/smoker temperature: 350°F.

steps.title: Garlic butter finish
steps.instruction: Mix melted butter with garlic, oregano, Parmesan, and red pepper flakes. Brush over tops and bake uncovered 8–10 minutes at 375°F until golden brown. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Game Day Pizza Sliders onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Slice and serve hot
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes, then slice along individual roll seams with a serrated knife. Serve with warm marinara for dunking while cheese is still stretchy.

proTips: Add a layer of cooked sausage crumbles if the crew wants meatier sliders.
Line pans with parchment plus foil so melted cheese releases cleanly.
Hold baked sliders covered at 200°F— they stay soft up to 45 minutes for late arrivals.
tonightSpread: Two pans of pizza sliders with warm marinara and a green salad.
Garlic knots or breadsticks from the store for extra carb coverage on long games.
leftovers: Reheat covered at 325°F until cheese remelts—good next-day lunch between shifts.
Cube and bake into a pizza bread pudding with eggs and more cheese.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sliders feed a crowd without plates or forks. One sheet pan makes twenty bites, they reheat fast, and everyone knows exactly how to eat them without a briefing.
mealPrepNotes: Assemble sliders in a foil-lined pan up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate. Add 5 minutes bake time from cold. Garlic butter can be melted and held warm in a squeeze bottle.
